text:
(Fantasy)


I went off, fists in my torn pockets...

my waistcoat too was becoming ideal,

walking beneath the open sky, Muse, I was so faithful to you!

how many great loves, ah ah ah, I dreamed myself!


My only pair of trousers was a huge tear.

—Dreaming Tom Thumb, I scattered on my way

rhymes. And my inn was the Great Bear.

—My stars trembled with a sweet rustle.


And I listened to them, at the roadside

when September evenings fall, feeling

dew on my forehead, like a wine of life.


And rhyming, lost, through fantastic shadows,

I stretched the laces, as if they were lyres,

of my torn shoes, beside my heart.

translation.title: My Bohemia
translation.editorial_note: The translation keeps the vagabond poet's torn pockets, star-inn, and shoes turned into lyres.
